endorsements.quote: Gate 0 therefore asks whether AI offers meaningful incremental value over explicit rules and whether representative data, valid labels, human oversight, lifecycle monitoring, and proportionate resources are available.
The platform needs a bounded intended purpose, target population, use environment, claims hierarchy, and evidence linking content to a plausible rationale.

Products that claim to prevent, manage, or treat a condition require an evidence and quality pathway proportionate to their intended use, including analytical and clinical evaluation, risk management, cybersecurity, maintenance, and post-market monitoring [ 11 , 12 , 13 ].

Safety requires explicit red flags, contraindications, medication boundaries, escalation and adverse-event procedures, limits of automated advice, and named responsibility for reviewing, overriding, suspending, or investigating system behavior.
Conflicts of interest should be disclosed, and independent assessment is preferable when conclusions are used beyond internal development.
Before model choice, teams should define the decision AI would support, the failure it would avoid, and the prespecified incremental benefit over explicit rules.

For the proposed AI, compare the same task and workload against the rule baseline, document the relevant system boundary and assumptions, measure energy or carbon where feasible, and avoid generic per-query estimates as product evidence.
Environmental effects require an explicit system boundary and should not be inferred from remote delivery [ 9 , 10 ].

unlisted_practices: Retain a simpler rule-based system when AI is unnecessary, ungovernable, or disproportionate, treating non-adoption as a legitimate outcome.
Do not claim environmental benefit of an AI or digital tool without measurement.
Do not allow self-management software to drift into diagnosis or treatment through wording, scores, or automated advice.
Replace unsupported claims of symptom improvement or personalization in user-facing text with bounded self-management descriptions.
Provide a clinically reviewed user-facing safety notice and referral instructions covering red-flag symptoms before public release of a self-management app.
Evaluate accessibility with representative users rather than inferring it from smartphone availability.
Do not accept unsupported verbal assurances as evidence in readiness assessments; require documented evidence attributable to a responsible owner.
Do not use an aggregate readiness score because strength in one domain cannot compensate for an unmet blocking condition in another.
Require claim-matched safety, ownership, accessibility, evidence, and lifecycle milestones in funding and procurement rather than AI inclusion alone.
Ensure a rule-based baseline is technically reliable, clinically justified, and prospectively evaluated before formal comparison with AI.
Obtain licensing authorization for validated questionnaires before public or research use of electronic versions.
Advance clinical claims only after the intervention, risk controls, workflows, and evaluation plan are fixed.

screen.reason: This is a perspective paper proposing a Responsible AI Readiness Framework for digital self-management platforms and applying it conceptually to a rule-based platform.
